findings.title: Materials' 49-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.13x forward but 35.41x trailing, a 49-point percentile gap between lenses. The market is pricing a 107 percent earnings surge that would erase most of the multiple compression, a bet on a cyclical rebound that has not yet shown up in reported numbers.

findings.title: Health Care's 99th percentile forward multiple is extreme
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E sits at the 99th percentile of its five-year range, up 24 points in a month, while trailing earnings justify only an 84th percentile rank. The 46 percent compression between lenses implies analysts expect 85 percent earnings growth, an unusually aggressive assumption for a sector already at historic valuation highs.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' month-long repricing defies its stability
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile jumped 81 points in a month to 87, a violent re-rating for a defensive sector whose trailing multiple barely moved. The market is now paying 21.20x forward for 36 percent implied earnings growth, a growth rate that clashes with the sector's reputation for steady, low-volatility profits.
